A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TOPF research by the same authors, despite the title changing from Node-Level to Point-Level. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original clustering accuracies and runtimes in Table 1, noise/outlier experiments in Figure 5, and qualitative feature extraction on synthetic and protein data.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds harmonic-projection ablations, sampling and parameter studies, runtime analyses, and cyclooctane and image-patch experiments.

M1.justification: The four-step TOPF pipeline remains. v2 adds an integer-program repair for generators whose Z/3Z-to-real lift is not a cycle, skipping features when repair is infeasible (Appendix B.3). Appendix G also introduces an alternative fixed-count feature-selection rule. These are localized procedural extensions.

E1.justification: The seven TCBS datasets and protein/Lorenz examples remain; Spheres+Grid becoming 4Circles+Grid does not establish new data. v2 adds cyclooctane conformation data and image-patch experiments in VAE latent spaces and raw image space. Neural comparisons also introduce ShapeNetPart and 3DMatch pretraining.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds PointNet and WSDesc and removes the Agglomerative Clustering column, although that comparator remains in the new sampling studies. Those studies additionally evaluate OPTICS and Mean Shift. The retained TPCC, spectral clustering, DBSCAN, ToMATo, geometric-feature, and node2vec comparisons remain.

E3.justification: v2 introduces random downsampling with a reported minimum of 16 points, asymmetric half-cloud downsampling by factors up to 100, parameter sweeps, and density-scaling runtime tests comparing automatic sparsification with sparsification disabled. These are new evaluation designs; the retained benchmark's ARI metric and default TOPF parameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained noise/outlier tests and weighting illustration, v2 adds a harmonic-projection ablation (Table 2), interpolation/threshold/feature-selection and clustering sensitivity analyses (Figure 10), sampling robustness studies (Figures 5, 15–16), and runtime scaling analysis (Figure 11). These directly test component necessity, parameter dependence, and practical robustness.

E5.justification: Both versions report 20 runs with means and standard deviations in Table 1 and 95% confidence intervals for noise/outlier results. v2 specifies 100 repetitions for the new sampling studies, with standard deviations explicitly reported in Figure 15. This does not establish increased repetitions for retained experiments.

E6.justification: Retained TOPF benchmark ARIs remain unchanged, including the 0.86 mean, while reported mean runtime changes from 17.5 to 15.1 seconds. v2 adds PointNet and WSDesc mean ARIs of 0.44 and 0.39. Table 2 reports 0.47 mean ARI without harmonic projection versus 0.86 with it, alongside substantial new sampling, sensitivity, runtime, and application results.

T1.justification: v1's alpha-filtration sphere theorem becomes Theorem C.1 primarily for alpha*, with additional circumsphere conditions for the implemented alpha filtration and an added contractible-subcomplex case. Definitions distinguish alpha*, Gabriel simplices, and alpha complexes, and the proof is extended. Appendix B also adds a continuous differential-form construction and mathematical treatment of failed real lifts.

C1.justification: The central TOPF contribution, benchmark novelty, and clustering-performance claims remain. v2 foregrounds robustness to heterogeneous sampling and adds an explicit conclusion about performance on very sparse datasets. The introduction also removes v1's blanket assertion that graph models cannot capture higher-order topological information.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations for projection-ablation exceptions on thin manifolds, downsampling failures on Ellipses and Spaceship, sampling-density robustness, and Python–Julia runtime overhead. It interprets pretrained neural comparisons through training-data requirements and qualifies VAE applications by the presence of meaningful topology. The original general limitations are largely retained.

D1.justification: v2 documents downstream spectral clustering, benchmark-label construction, WSDesc implementation and keypoint settings, VAE feature-selection settings, and automatic landmark/random subsampling. Existing package access and hardware disclosures remain. Some new details conflict: Section 4 reports 518 image patches, while Figure 12 reports 578; reported raw-image dimensions are also inconsistent.

R1.justification: Related work expands substantially to local topological signatures, multiparameter representations, Mapper, topological autoencoders, topological node2vec, and adversarial graph representations. Appendix A explicitly positions TOPF's localization of global topology against methods that preserve topology during embedding or compute local and global summaries separately.

P1.justification: Most existing exposition remains. Editorial changes include the Point-Level title, localized shortening and rewording, moving the main theorem from Section 4 to Appendix C, and repartitioning appendix material. New scientific sections expand the document without a wholesale rewrite of the retained narrative.

P2.justification: v2 adds an ablation table and numerous application, sensitivity, sampling, and runtime figures, and changes Table 1's comparator columns. Earlier Figures 2–3 are combined, the qualitative overview gains a VAE panel, and noise/outlier panels are enlarged and reversed. Some captions deteriorate: Figure 3 retains an editing note, and Figure 6 misidentifies its left/right panels.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation that was missing in v1: Table 2 tests harmonic projection, Figure 10 tests parameter sensitivity, and sampling studies and high-dimensional applications probe practical scope. The revised theorem states additional conditions for the implemented filtration, and the lifting repair addresses an overlooked procedural case. These gains outweigh the conflicting VAE details and caption errors, although those defects limit reproducibility and polish.
